# lua-slds

> Short Link Domain Specification (SLDS) — a pure Lua domain library defining short link identity, lifecycle, and resolution semantics.

## What is SLDS?

SLDS defines what a short link **is** (identity), how it **behaves** (lifecycle), and what it **means** to resolve one (resolution semantics), independent of transport, storage, caching, and security policy.

- Core layer: zero external dependencies, pure Lua 5.1 / 5.3 / LuaJIT
- Architecture: hexagonal (ports and adapters)
- Specification: 10 iron rules + conformance test suite (L0-L3)

## Installation

```
luarocks install lua-slds
```

## Quick Start

```lua
local slds = require("slds")
local service = slds.new({
    repository = require("slds.adapters.inmemory.repository").new(),
    generator  = require("slds.adapters.sequential.generator").new(),
    encoder    = require("slds.adapters.base62.encoder").new(),
})
local link = service:create({}, { target = "https://example.com" })
local result = service:resolve({}, slds.Identity.new("default", link.code))
print(result.target, result.status)
```

## Core Concepts

- Identity = { namespace, code } — logically immutable ordinary Lua table; callers must not rewrite fields
- ShortLink = { namespace, code, target, status, expires_at } — domain entity
- Lifecycle = ACTIVE <-> DISABLED -> DELETED (terminal); EXPIRED is derived at resolution time
- Resolution = first-class domain operation, returns ResolutionResult (not ShortLink)
- Ports = Repository, Generator, Encoder (interface contracts, hexagonal)
- Hooks = synchronous observers with per-callback domain snapshots and pcall exception isolation; ctx stays shared
- Metadata = opaque raw-table snapshots; no business schema, metadata patch or deep merge
- Repository update = atomic sparse patch against latest state; DELETED cannot be revived
- Sequential/Base62 = bundled adapters with integer domain [0, 2^53-1]; generic ports remain representation-agnostic

## 10 Iron Rules

1. Core MUST NOT depend on HTTP
2. Core MUST NOT depend on a specific database
3. Core MUST NOT fetch Target URLs
4. Code MUST be immutable after creation
5. Code uniqueness MUST be enforced atomically by persistence layer
6. Deleted Codes MUST NOT be reused by default
7. Resolve MUST NOT require external event system
8. Analytics MUST NOT be in resolution critical path
9. Authorization MUST be outside Core Domain
10. Any implementation MUST pass Conformance Test Suite

## API

- slds.new({ repository, generator, encoder, clock?, hooks? }) -> Service
- service:create(ctx, input) -> ShortLink, err
- service:resolve(ctx, identity) -> ResolutionResult | nil, err
- service:update(ctx, identity, patch) -> ShortLink, err
- service:delete(ctx, identity) -> boolean, err
- service:use(hook) -> Service (chainable)
- slds.Identity.new(namespace, code) -> Identity

## Verification

- sh scripts/test.sh — fresh LuaCov statistics, >=95% line coverage for every src/ and adapters/ Lua file
- luacheck src/ adapters/ spec/ scripts/check-coverage.lua
- Reference conformance uses real adapters and deterministic interleavings; external concurrency and optional cache/tenant behavior require separate evidence
- docs/validation.md — runtime matrix, per-file results and migration notes

## Key Files

- src/slds/init.lua — module entry, public API
- src/slds/domain/ — Identity, ShortLink, Lifecycle, Resolution, Errors
- src/slds/ports/ — Repository, Generator, Encoder port interfaces
- src/slds/service.lua — Application Service
- src/slds/hooks.lua — Hooks mechanism
- adapters/ — InMemory Repository, Sequential Generator, Base62 Encoder
- spec/ — busted BDD tests + conformance L0-L3
- docs/rfc/RFC-0001.md — full specification
